# Prompt Audit

> [!CAUTION]
> **Purpose:** Each prompt the product sends to a model — clear, well structured, and written for the model that runs it, per that model maker's current prompting guide.
>
> **Rules:**
>
> - Read-only audit; NEVER edit code, config, or data.
> - `Universal Instructions` apply to ALL projects; `Project Instructions` apply ONLY to this project.
> - Local audit instructions / overrides → `Project Instructions` below the bkit-managed block; universal instructions stay in-block.
> - Any tools mentioned in `Universal Instructions` are examples only; swap for actual tools in final output; drop inapplicable.
> - Use dense token-efficient phrasing; NO filler / hedging / restating; tables > prose, bullets > paragraphs.
> - Read `.agents/docs.md` → load docs for workflow / step / task; skip missing; cite docs inline where required.
> - Every claim cites evidence (`file:line`, or command / query and its output) and tool behind it.
> - Read this document ONCE at session start; do NOT trust session memory; do NOT re-read on every loop iteration.
> - Quote at most one line of prompt text per finding; NEVER copy personal data or a model completion into the report.
> - NEVER call a model to generate. Token counts use a local tokenizer or a provider count endpoint only.

## Universal Instructions

### Context & Goals

A prompt is written against one model maker's advice at one point in time. The model behind it changes, the advice changes, and the prompt does not. Rules pile up without reasons, emphasis written for an older model makes a newer one over-apply a rule, the output format drifts from the parser that reads it. Nothing fails a test: the model still answers, a little worse. Target failure: **a prompt that the current guide for the model running it says will degrade results, and nobody re-read it after the model or the guide changed.**

**Applies when:** the product sends a prompt to a language model at runtime (system prompt, message template, few-shot examples, tool or output-schema descriptions). Coding-agent instruction files and bkit-managed files are not product prompts. None → one `N/A` row with evidence, never "clean".

**Cadence:** quarterly. Extra pass after a model change at any call site (`bkit-audit-models`), a new prompt set, or a maker guide update.

**Anchor Standards:** record URL, last-updated date or date read, and the model generation each targets. Newer version → `Standards` step reads what changed.

- Anthropic prompt engineering docs and the prompting best-practices page for current Claude models.
- OpenAI prompt engineering guide and the model-specific prompting guide for each model in use (e.g. the cookbook guide per model generation).
- Google Gemini API prompt design strategies.
- Every other maker whose model runs a prompt (e.g. xAI, Mistral, Meta, DeepSeek, Qwen): its own prompting guide, or `Not Checked` when it publishes none.
- Each maker's tool-use and structured-output docs, for tool and schema descriptions.

Guides disagree. The guide for the model that runs the prompt wins. A prompt that runs on models from more than one maker (fallback chain, router, several hosts) relies only on practice every one of those guides supports.

### Scope

- Every runtime prompt: system prompt, message template, few-shot set, prefill, tool descriptions, output-schema descriptions.
- Model and guide per prompt.
- Clarity: task, success, context and reason behind each rule, definitions, contradictions, dead instructions.
- Structure: sections, delimiters, ordering, examples, output format against its parser.
- Model fit: emphasis, reasoning and verbosity controls, sampling parameters, prefill, workarounds from an older model.
- Tool and output-schema descriptions.
- Token cost, duplication, cache-friendly ordering.
- Deliberate departures from a guide: recorded once, not re-raised.

### Out of Scope

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Excluded item | Why | Where it belongs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Injection boundary, tool capability, output validators, call limits, evals / golden sets | LLM sweep | `bkit-audit-llm` |
| Model choice, deprecation, catalogue, fallback-chain membership | Model sweep | `bkit-audit-models` |
| Coding-agent instruction files (e.g. `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, agent definitions, skills): loading, permissions, untrusted input | Agent config sweep | `bkit-audit-agents` |
| Contradictions between instruction files; always-loaded size | Documentation sweep | `bkit-audit-documentation` |
| bkit-managed prompts and templates (`.bkit/`, `bkit-*` host agent mirrors, `bkit:start` / `bkit:end` blocks) | Fixed upstream in bkit | bkit's own run of this audit |
| Live hostile probes | Red team | `bkit-audit-red-team` |
| Model spend beyond per-call token count | Cost sweep | `bkit-audit-cost` |
| Rewriting prompts | Audit reports only | Plan from this report |

## Findings

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Severity | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `CRITICAL` | Output-format instruction contradicts the parser or schema that consumes it on a write path, so following the prompt writes wrong data or drops it |
| `HIGH` | Model changed and the prompt keeps practice the current guide says degrades results; contradictory instructions in one prompt; output format unstated where code parses it; write tool with no when-to-use or parameter meaning; sampling parameter or prefill the model rejects |
| `MEDIUM` | Rule with no reason where the guide asks for one; examples missing where format matters, or contradicting instructions; prompt on several makers' models relying on one maker's behaviour; fixed content after variable content where the provider caches; text duplicated across prompts; dead instruction; departure from a guide not recorded |
| `LOW` | Wording; token waste with no behaviour change; non-write tool description gaps |

Scale per `.bkit/jsonl.md` § Severity. Within a severity: write paths first, then prompts whose model changed. A departure recorded in `docs/decisions.jsonl` with a reason is not a finding.

## Report

### Summary

- **Run:** baseline, 2026-10-09, HEAD `a9b9b06693aabe52020445b209b955fc3170f9bc`. Scope per `Project Instructions`: the 48 subagent prompts in `.bkit/prompts/*.md`, all read in full.
- **Findings:** 13 — `CRITICAL` 0 · `HIGH` 3 · `MEDIUM` 6 · `LOW` 4. Every `Verify` = `unverified` (no eval set exists).
- **Models:** 13 models from 7 makers across 7 provider columns (`.bkit/prompts.md:163-212`): Anthropic (`claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5`), xAI (`cursor-grok-4.5-high`), Cursor (`composer-2.5`), DeepSeek (`deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`), Moonshot (`kimi-k2.7-code`, `kimi-k3`), Z.ai (`glm-5.3-flash`), OpenAI (`gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-6-luna`; column provisional). Every prompt runs on all 7 makers → the multi-maker rule applies to every prompt.
- **Guides read (all 2026-10-09; no page publishes a last-updated date):** Anthropic Prompting best practices + Prompting Claude Opus 5.5 / Opus 5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Sonnet 5 / Haiku 5.5 (+ Fable 5 for context, not pinned); OpenAI Prompting guidance for GPT-5.6 Sol, Using GPT-6, Rethinking skills and prompts for GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5 prompting guide (older generation, context); Moonshot Best Practices for Prompts + Kimi K3 page; DeepSeek Thinking Mode (parameters only); Z.ai Migrate to GLM-5.3 + Coding Agents best practice; Cursor Models + Rules docs (host guidance only). Unread: xAI (guide URL HTTP 404, no Grok 4.5 guide), Cursor Composer / DeepSeek / Z.ai wording guidance (none published) → `Not Checked`.
- **For tracker issue #501 (capitals, `NEVER` vs `do NOT`, bold, one-clause reasons), from Steps 3 and 6:**
  - **Capitals:** OpenAI GPT-5.6 reserves `ALWAYS` / `NEVER` / `must` / `only` for true invariants and asks for decision rules on judgement calls; Anthropic says to dial back aggressive language on current Claude models; GPT-6 Astra may stop work over boundaries written for older models. No guide read supports capitals on judgement calls. About 60% of the 1,021 capitalised normative words sit on process / judgement lines → `prompts-3` (`HIGH`).
  - **`NEVER` vs `do NOT`:** no guide distinguishes the two. OpenAI groups `NEVER` with the invariant markers; Anthropic prefers saying what to do over either form. Consistent with every guide: capitalised `NEVER` only on invariants, plain lower-case "do not" elsewhere; mixed-case "do NOT" adds emphasis without marking a tier.
  - **Bold:** no guide read addresses bold in prompts. Structural bold (clause labels, `**If**`, `**Create**`; 1,169 of 1,217 bold spans) is neutral. Emphasis bold is only the `⛔` STOP line, which also breaks the house rule → `prompts-10` (`LOW`).
  - **One-clause reasons:** Anthropic recommends giving the reason ("Claude is smart enough to generalize from the explanation"); OpenAI GPT-5.6 neither asks for nor forbids reasons; Moonshot asks for detail and context; no guide supports banning them. The `NO rationale` rule (`.bkit/prompts.md:37`) is a recorded deliberate choice that departs from the Anthropic guide → listed in `Deliberate Choices`, not a finding (record exists; no evidence the guide changed after the rule was written). No guide read opposes a one-clause reason on a rule a model would otherwise misread or over-apply, and Anthropic's asks for it; `bkit-ship-conflict-resolve.md:45` is the one prompt that already carries one.
- **Other `HIGH`:** `prompts-1` (`git add -A` inside a prompt that forbids `git add`), `prompts-2` (a review-only prompt told to add plan tasks).

### Structure

Shared across all 48 (Read): sections delimited by bold clause labels, a `[!CAUTION]` block and a fenced Output format (G7: markdown sections accepted by every guide read); instructions apart from data — inputs arrive as file paths in the invocation message and their content enters through tool results, never interpolated into the prompt (injection handling → `bkit-audit-llm`); long-input placement n/a (no inline documents); structured output / tool schema n/a (outputs are markdown files written with Write / Edit / `echo >>`; the host subagent layer offers no response schema); verdict vocabularies match their consumers (test-gated by `.bkit/src/bkit-verdict-vocabulary.test.ts`). Examples: `T` = literal output template only (DC7), `T+E` = template plus worked examples. Consumer lines from rg ``until `<!-- verdict:end -->` `` over `.bkit/workflows/*.md`.

### Tools and Schemas

Skipped — surface absent. No prompt defines a tool, parameter schema or JSON output schema: rg `input_schema|inputSchema|registerTool|server\.tool\(|"parameters"\s*:` over `.bkit/src`, `.bkit/prompts`, `.bkit/scripts` → no hits. Frontmatter `tools:` only allowlists host built-ins (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`), `mcp__serena__*`, and in `bkit-utility-update-roadmap.md:13-25` tracker MCP reads — their descriptions belong to the host or MCP server, not to bkit. Output shapes are markdown templates, judged under `Structure`. Tool capability and bounds → `bkit-audit-llm`.

### Efficiency

Token counts: Anthropic `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` (no generation), prompt body after frontmatter sent as `system` with each prompt's pinned model, minus a 9-token baseline. Claude tokenizer only — other makers `Not Checked`. `Protocol` = the `> ` lines (`[!CAUTION]` EXECUTION PROTOCOL block + `⛔` STOP lines) counted the same way: 18,316 of 80,968 tokens (22.6%) across the 48. Each agent loads only its own file, so cross-prompt duplication costs maintenance, not per-call tokens; the per-call cost of the shared block is its share of each prompt.

Cache order: PASS for all 48 — the rendered agent body is the fixed system prompt (`.claude/agents/`, `.cursor/agents/`, `.opencode/agents/`, `.codex/agents/*.toml` `developer_instructions`); variable `Context` / `Read` / `Create` lines arrive in the invocation message after it; prompts carry no orchestrator-substituted `{VAR}` (`.bkit/prompts.md:29`).

Duplication groups (diff / rg): protocol block in 48 (restates `.agents/rules.md` clauses — DC3); `Destructive git PROHIBITED` clause in 8; memory-hygiene step in 6 (`rg -c "Ensure agent memories"`); summaries' `Recommended Next Step` `<ref>` paragraph in 5; near-twins `bkit-utility-update-deferrals` / `-failures` (7 of 76 lines differ), `-decisions` / `-knowledge` (7 of 75), `bkit-plan-scope-check-1` / `-2` (identical but `name` / `model` — deliberate diversity pair, `.bkit/prompts.md:24`). Self-contained prompts are deliberate (`.bkit/prompts.md:40`) → not findings.

**(b) Senior prompt-engineer pass:**

1. **Audit / plan template gate boilerplate** — `.bkit/templates/docs/templates/` (35 files): `**CRITICAL AI AGENT INSTRUCTION:** 🛑 CHECKPOINT` + `**DO NOT stop for user permission.**` on 106 gate lines, `🚨` headings in all 35, `**CRITICAL:**` 42 times (rg). An agent reads these as prompt text (this run read them as instructions). **Verdict:** the intent — tick the boxes, then continue without asking — is supported by every guide read (`O-56` stopping conditions; `A-O55` names the unwanted stops); the form is not: it is the "CRITICAL: You MUST" wording `A-BP` says to dial back and capitals on a non-invariant that `O-56` reserves for invariants. A plain line ("Tick each box once it holds, then continue to `Probe Steps` without asking.") keeps the instruction. Scope for that edit: bkit-managed templates, so `bkit-audit-documentation` / a #501 follow-up, not this audit.
2. **The style lives in `.agents/rules.md` too.** Every prompt makes its agent read it (`**Rules:**` bullet), and it carries the same capitals density (e.g. `.agents/rules.md:21-32`). A #501 change limited to `.bkit/prompts/` leaves agents reading the old style one hop away. Coding-agent instruction files are outside this audit (`bkit-audit-agents`).
3. **`bkit-utility-compress-markdown` encodes the capitals convention.** `.agents/rules.md:164` makes every prose edit apply its Process. It protects only capitalised normative keywords (`:48` inventory and per-section counts, `:59` "survive verbatim"), so a rule rewritten in plain case under #501 ("do not …") loses that protection and can be paraphrased or merged by a later compression run. A #501 change needs a matching edit there (protect plain-case prohibitions too).
4. **Effort table drift (documentation, not prompts):** `.bkit/providers.md:128` maps OpenCode `high`→`medium`, `xhigh`→`high` and says Cursor does not support `effort`; `.bkit/prompts.md:79-85` (parsed by install) maps `high`→`max`, `xhigh`→`max` and Cursor identity. Install follows `.bkit/prompts.md`; the providers doc is stale → `bkit-audit-documentation`.
5. **`reasoning_extraction` watch.** Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 run a classifier that declines prompts pushing the model to reproduce internal reasoning (`A-O55`, `A-S55` § Safeguard refusals). bkit's `#### Reason` / `Verdict Reasoning` sections ask for short explanations, which the guides allow; a decline would surface as `stop_reason: "refusal"` and an empty or partial artifact. No incident in the ledgers (rg). Worth a golden case.
6. **Maker changelogs since the last run (baseline: current state):** the Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 pages are the current guides for the pinned models; their prompt-relevant changes (effort recalibrated, `medium` default on Opus 5.5, thinking always on, progress updates as thinking blocks, new refusal classifiers) are covered by MF2, MF7, MF8. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra guidance ("fewer rules, not more") lands on the same point as `prompts-3`. No step would have caught that the OpenAI column is unprobed (`.bkit/prompts.md:150`) — Model Fit for OpenAI rests on guides alone.
7. **WebFetch summarisation.** On some hosts the fetch tool returns a summary and refuses verbatim passages over ~125 characters; per-topic short-quote questions and `.md` page variants (OpenAI docs) worked. Recorded in `Project Instructions`.

### Process Improvements

**Universal** (proposed template step changes; template above `bkit:end` untouched):

- **Step 5 — Structure:** add "every header field a consumer parses has a Process step that sets it and says what it counts; every field the Process asks for appears in the Output format" (caught `prompts-4`, `-6`, `-12`; a field-to-step cross-check is mechanical).
- **Step 6 — Model Fit:** before judging emphasis, classify each capitalised absolute as invariant (safety, permission, required field, irreversible action) or judgement call; judge only the second group. Raw counts overstate the problem (40% of this repo's capitals sit on invariant lines).
- **Step 3 — Guides:** when a maker publishes no prompting guide or its URL is dead, still read its parameter docs (reasoning-effort values, rejected sampling parameters) so Step 6 parameter checks run instead of falling to `Not Checked`.
- **Pre-Flight Web:** note that fetch tools may summarise and cap verbatim quotes; fallback = per-topic short-quote questions or the page's `.md` variant.

**Project** (applied below `bkit:end` in `docs/templates/bkit-audit-prompts.md`):

- `Scope (Step 2)` adds `.codex/agents/` to the skipped renders; added `Call sites / renders (Step 2)`, `Consumers (Step 5)`, `Emphasis (Step 6)`, `Tokens (Step 8)`, `Guides (Step 3)`, `Tool gaps (Pre-Flight Web)`, `Evals (Step 9)`, `Gate boilerplate (Step 11)`; `Deliberate choices (Step 9)` extended with where the other recorded choices live.

**Golden cases proposed to `bkit-audit-llm`** (no eval set exists; one per finding): `prompts-1` remediation never stages unrelated files · `prompts-2` scope-check leaves the plan byte-identical · `prompts-3` capitalised vs plain process lines, same task, per tier · `prompts-4` reviewers report `Failures` = `CRITICAL` count · `prompts-5` six open questions survive verbatim · `prompts-6` trailing `BLOCKED —` → `FAIL` · `prompts-7` one addressable gap → mapped verdict · `prompts-8` two doc edits listed · `prompts-9` Opus 5.5 with vs without the final re-read step · `prompts-10`–`13` covered by the cases above or wording-only · effort sweep per tier on bkit tasks (DC6) · `reasoning_extraction` refusal check on `bkit-debug-failure-diagnose` (Beyond the Steps 5).

**Proposed `docs/decisions.jsonl` rows** (not written — read-only audit):

- Reason clauses in prompts — record the #501 outcome (keep the `NO rationale` ban, or allow one clause on rules a model would misread or over-apply) with the guide comparison from `Deliberate Choices` DC2.
- No worked examples in prompt output formats (DC7): literal templates fix the shape; examples only where judgement needs calibration (as in the challenge class lists).
